text:
nina: FYI getting a spike in failed dedicated allocs in us-west1 since ~10:12 UTC — looks like we hit a regional GPU quota wall for dedicated pools
ops-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-alloc-failures us-west1 10:12 -> 10:20 (95% local quota used)
kai: ugh, those are the host pools for prod-dedicated, right? any noisy tenant causing this?
nina: not obvious from first glance — allocation logs show a lot of small, bursty jobs from a handful of tenants and some long-running warm pools reclaiming slots
sam: if we spill to us-west2 we should expect ~8-20ms extra p99 for some customers. also egress costs will bump for data-sensitive tenants :grimacing:
marta: we could do a temporary routing tweak: prefer cross-region spill for non-SLA tenants and keep SLA-tagged traffic local. simple policy change, revert when quota replenishes.
kaI: (cc @marta) can you paste the quick example of the policy? want to run it as a canary first.
marta: sure — sample routing rule (canary window):
```
{
  "match": {
    "tenant_tier": "standard",
    "region": "us-west1"
  },
  "action": {
    "route_to": "us-west2",
    "max_extra_latency_ms": 25,
    "tag": "temp-spill-2025-07-01"
  }
}
```
devon: we should also throttle bursty warm-pool reclaimers — those are probably hogging dedicated slices. maybe add a soft backoff in the allocator.
nina: agreed. i want two parallel mitigations: 1) route-standard->us-west2 canary for 5% of traffic immediately, 2) deploy allocator soft-backoff to dampen reclaims over 30s windows.
sam: cost/billing question: do we have approval to accept extra egress for that canary? sales/customer-ops needs heads-up for any enterprise tenants that have locality requirements. :phone: 
marta: i'll ping solutions and pricing. for the canary we can set `max_extra_latency_ms` and limit to low % — should be fine under current cost budget, but confirm.
ops-bot: [INFO] created incident 12544: "us-west1-dedicated-quota-spill" — assignees: eng-infra oncall, quota-team
kai: timeline: can we roll the canary in 10 min and monitor p99+ errors and alloc success rate? if we see regressions, rollback to strict-local routing.
devon: +1. i'll push the allocator soft-backoff patch to staging and wire the metric `allocator.reclaim_rate` -> alert if > 3/s per pool.
nina: i'll run a quick query vs recent 2h: `count(failed_allocs{region="us-west1"}) by tenant` and share top-5.
sam: also add a check for KV cache warmup misses — cross-region spill may hit cold cache so observe token-latency regressions separately.
marta: log the rollback plan in the incident: revert tag "temp-spill-2025-07-01" and remove routing rule. i'll draft the two-line playbook in the runbook.
ops-bot: [INFO] canary policy applied to 5% of standard tenants -> routes to us-west2 (tag=temp-spill-2025-07-01)
kai: monitoring dashboards: p99 latency, failed_alloc_rate, egress_bytes, allocator.reclaim_rate. set an automated rollback if failed_alloc_rate increases or p99 > baseline + 30ms.
devon: pushed soft-backoff to staging. ready to promote to canary after 2 green runs.
nina: action items: (1) canary route -> us-west2 5% (marta) (2) soft-backoff allocator canary (devon) (3) notify sales/solutions about potential latency/egress (marta) (4) monitor and auto-rollback thresholds (kai)
sam: thanks — keep thread updated with dashboards/links. i'll standby for impact notice to customers if needed. :thumbsup:
